name: A01 evenBackslashesBefore: the parity inverted
why: every escaped hash reads as a closing run and every real one as escaped: the stated rows and every enumeration fail

name: A02 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk reads a slash, not a backslash
why: no run is ever seen, so every character reads as unescaped

name: A03 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk stops one character short of the start
why: a backslash at index 0 is never counted: `\#` reads as a closing run

name: A04 evenBackslashesBefore: only a zero run is even
why: a run of two backslashes reads as escaping: `a \\#` is refused

name: A05 evenBackslashesBefore: the parity taken mod 4
why: a run of two backslashes reads as odd

name: A06 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk capped at 64 characters
why: a run of 101 backslashes reads as 64 (even): the grid's 101 and the long-run rows

name: A07 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk capped at 4,096 characters
why: only a long ODD run is misread: the 4,097-backslash row of the oracle file (the old patterns are far too slow to compare there)

name: A08 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk capped at 65,536 characters
why: only a run past 65,536 is misread: the 65,537 and 1,000,001 rows

name: A09 evenBackslashesBefore: the walk reads the character AT the index, not before it
why: the character at the index is the hash or the brace, never a backslash: every run reads as even

name: A10 evenBackslashesBefore: the run counted from the start of the text for every call (a quadratic with a small constant)
why: every answer is the same; `headingAttributeStart` asks once per escaped brace, so 50,000 of them cost about 2.5e9 steps (each call counts back from its own index): the control row of 50,000 escaped braces fails on the clock alone

name: C01 atxClosingPandocStart: the run is made of dollar signs
why: no hash run is ever found

name: C02 atxClosingPandocStart: trimEnd() for the trailing blanks
why: a CR, a no-break space or a line separator after the run reads as a blank: the wide enumeration and the stated rows

name: C03 atxClosingPandocStart: the trailing blanks are not trimmed
why: `a #  ` is not a closing run

name: C04 atxClosingPandocStart: the hash walk stops at index 1
why: a text that is all hashes starts its run at 1, not 0

name: C05 atxClosingPandocStart: a text with no hash run is not refused
why: the start index of the (empty) run is answered for every text with no hash run

name: C06 atxClosingPandocStart: the parity negated
why: escaped and unescaped hashes swap

name: C07 atxClosingPandocStart: the second hash also taken for a run of ONE
why: `a \#` answers an index past the only hash

name: C08 atxClosingPandocStart: the second hash needs a run of THREE
why: `\##` (an escaped hash and a closing one) is refused

name: C09 atxClosingPandocStart: the third hash, not the second
why: `\##` answers 3, not 2

name: C10 atxClosingPandocStart: an escaped single hash answers its own index
why: `a \#` is read as a closing run

name: C11 atxClosingPandocStart: an escaped first hash never falls back to the second
why: `\##` is refused

name: C12 atxClosingPandocStart: the unescaped run answers its second hash
why: every closing run keeps its first hash

name: C13 atxClosingPandocStart: the parity read at the END of the run
why: the run before the last character is the run of hashes, always even

name: C14 atxClosingPandocStart: the parity read after the first hash
why: the character before is the hash itself, always even

name: C15 atxClosingPandocStart: the hash walk starts at the end of the text, not at the end of the blanks
why: trailing blanks stop the walk at once, so `a #  ` has no run

name: C16 atxClosingPandocStart: a blank accepted inside the hash walk
why: `# #` starts its run at 0

name: D01 atxClosingRun: the two spellings swapped
why: gfm strips an unspaced `C#` and the markdown family does not: the older heading rows of qmd-model.test.ts

name: D02 atxClosingRun: the pandoc spelling for every reader
why: gfm, commonmark and commonmark_x strip an unspaced `C#`

name: D03 atxClosingCommonmarkStart: the space before the run not required
why: `C#` loses its hash under gfm

name: H01 headingAttributeStart: the last character must be an opening brace
why: no block is ever found

name: H02 headingAttributeStart: a lone closing brace is not refused up front
why: EQUIVALENT: text `}` has its closing brace at index 0, the search for the previous brace clamps to index 0 and finds the brace itself, and no `{` follows; the answer is -1 either way

name: H03 headingAttributeStart: an empty block `{}` is refused
why: `{}` has its closing brace at index 1

name: H04 headingAttributeStart: the last character must NOT be a closing brace
why: every block is refused and every non-block accepted

name: H05 headingAttributeStart: trimEnd() for the trailing blanks
why: a CR, a no-break space or a line separator after the block reads as a blank

name: H06 headingAttributeStart: the search for the opening brace starts AT the previous closing brace
why: EQUIVALENT: the character at that index is a `}`, not a `{`, and with no previous brace the index is -1, which `indexOf` clamps to 0

name: H07 headingAttributeStart: the search starts two characters after the previous closing brace
why: a `{` right after a `}` is skipped: `a }{x}`

name: H08 headingAttributeStart: the previous closing brace looked for from the last one itself
why: the last brace is its own predecessor, so the search for an opening brace starts past the end: no block is ever found

name: H09 headingAttributeStart: the FIRST closing brace of the text, not the one before the last
why: a `{` between two earlier braces is taken for the start: `{a}{b}{c}`

name: H10 headingAttributeStart: the loop also stops at the closing brace
to: open !== -1 && open < close; open = text.indexOf("{", open + 1))
why: EQUIVALENT: no `{` lies at or after the last non-blank character, which is a `}`

name: H11 headingAttributeStart: after an escaped brace the next one is skipped
why: `a \{{x}`: the brace right after an escaped one is the answer

name: H12 headingAttributeStart: the parity not asked
why: an escaped brace opens a block: `a \{x}`

name: H13 headingAttributeStart: the answer is the character after the brace
why: every block starts one character late

name: H14 headingAttributeStart: the LAST brace of the line, not the first one after the previous closing brace
from: for (let open = text.indexOf("{", text.lastIndexOf("}", close - 1) + 1); open !== -1;
why: `a {{x}` answers 3, not 2

name: H15 headingAttributeStart: the parity read after the brace
why: the character before is the brace itself: always even

name: W01 buildHeading: the attribute text taken from one character after the brace
why: SURVIVED the first rows (46 killed, 5 survived in the first run): a block text read one character late differs only when the heading has exactly TWO opening braces (`# T {{#a}`), which no row held; killed by the WIRING rows added after that run (the parent's answers for 24 headings, `heading-tail-equivalence.test.ts`)

name: W02 buildHeading: the cut keeps the opening brace
why: a block leaves its `{` in the text

name: W03 buildHeading: the closing cut keeps the first hash
why: a closing run leaves its first hash in the text

name: W04 buildHeading: a closing run at index 0 is not cut
why: an all-hash heading (`## ##`) is kept instead of dropped

name: W05 buildHeading: the attribute index tested with < 0
why: EQUIVALENT: the locator answers -1 or an index

name: W06 buildHeading: the attribute block looked for under every reader
why: gfm and markdown_github render a trailing `{...}` as text

name: W07 buildHeading: the closing run located in the RAW text, attribute block included
why: a closing run before an attribute block (`a ## {#x}`) is not found
